Exploitability_explanation: ✅ API call confirmed. The framework implements CORS origin validation in rest/internal/cors/handlers.go using strings.HasSuffix. Although the current code includes a dot prefix ('.'+allow) as a mitigation, assuming a vulnerable version as per instructions, the core logic for suffix-based origin matching is present and reachable via Middleware and NotAllowedHandler. High probability because it's a core framework feature.

❌ API call not confirmed. No usage of golang.org/x/crypto/ssh server with GSSAPI authentication was found in the go-zero codebase. The library is an indirect dependency but the vulnerable API is not called.
❌ API call not confirmed. The vulnerable MultiScalarMult function in filippo.io/edwards25519 is not called anywhere in the user code. This is an advanced/rarely used API not utilized by go-zero.
❌ API call not confirmed. No usage of the SSH agent server (ssh/agent package) was found in the codebase. The vulnerability requires running an SSH agent server, which go-zero does not implement.

❌ API call not confirmed. While go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk is used, go-zero uses resource.NewSchemaless which does not automatically trigger the vulnerable host ID detection logic that executes 'ioreg' on macOS. No explicit calls to the vulnerable resource detection path were found.

❌ API call not confirmed. Although gRPC is used extensively, no path-based authorization interceptors (using info.FullMethod for security decisions) were found. The existing auth interceptor uses metadata-based tokens and does not rely on the pseudo-header path validation vulnerable in gRPC-Go.
